title: Investment & Approval
goal: Make the money case, secure funding and people in tranches, clear the blockers and commit explicitly.

processes.title: Investment & Approval
processes.summary: Business case, funding, risk and conditions — and the Commitment gate: Go, Phase, Rework, Escalate or No-go.

definition.purpose: Make the money case, secure funding and people in tranches, clear the blockers and commit explicitly.
definition.outcome: A validated business case, tranche-1 funding, accepted risk with conditions and a recorded commitment decision; on Go or Phase, the committed initiative handed to DESIGN.
definition.jtbd: Help us commit money and people with confidence — and be able to explain why later.
exit: On Go / Phase: committed initiative pack accepted by DESIGN

flow.stateTransitions: Case drafted → Funded → Conditions set → Committed

cases.happyPath: Case positive at low benefits; tranche 1 within the sponsor's limit → Phase.
edgeCases: Mandated initiative — the decision is about how, not whether
exceptions: Decider unavailable → delegate per the authority matrix

routing.alternate: Phase → commit tranche 1; later tranches return to the gate
routing.escalation: Above the sponsor's limit or disputed → portfolio board
routing.stop: No-go → record and notify; Park → park record with revisit trigger — both recorded in the learning log

criteria: Benefits and costs as ranges with a do-nothing option
rules: No DESIGN or BUILD spend without a commitment record
Outcomes are Go, Phase, Rework, Escalate or No-go

roles: C — Finance partner, Risk owner, Legal, Engineering lead
execution.authority: Sponsor commits within their limit; portfolio board above it.

continuity.handoff: Commitment decision record and committed initiative pack → DESIGN; learning log and retrospective → EVOLVE
traceability: Creates BC-## and CMT-##; CMT links BC, the baseline version, RMP and RSK
measures: Tranche releases on evidence vs on schedule
learning: PLAN retrospective; park revisit dates tracked

lessons.title: Build the Business Case
lessons.summary: Show, with ranges, why this investment beats its alternatives.

definition.purpose: Show, with ranges, why this investment is worth more than its alternatives.
definition.outcome: A business case: options, benefits, costs, NPV and payback as ranges, sensitivities and a benefit owner.
definition.jtbd: Help me make the money case honestly enough that finance would sign it.
entry: Discovery cost estimate and sizing model
exit: Benefits and costs as ranges with sources
At least three options including do nothing

normal: Restate the need and the outcomes
Appraise options: do nothing, buy, build, hybrid
Model benefits with ramp-up by site
Model build and run costs from the forecast

cases.happyPath: NPV positive even at the low end of benefits.
alternates: Mandatory change → the case shows the least-cost compliant option
edgeCases: Benefit relies on redeploying clerks' time
exceptions: Finance disputes a benefit → move it to 'unquantified' and re-run
failures: Benefits counted at the high end only

routing.rework: Model gaps → back to estimate or roadmap inputs
routing.escalation: Finance and sponsor disagree on assumptions → CFO / portfolio board
routing.stop: NPV negative at likely values → recommend no-go — recorded in the learning log

checks: Sensitivity on the top three inputs
rules: Costs include three years of run
policies: Investment appraisal per finance policy (discount rate, horizon)

decisions: Is it worth it, and which option

roles: C — Finance partner, Engineering lead, Procurement
execution.authority: Finance validates the model; the sponsor owns the case.

continuity.handoff: Business case, benefits model and options appraisal → 2.5.2 Secure Funding & Resourcing
traceability: Creates BC-## linked to OPP-###, EST-## and the forecast

workflows.title: Build the Business Case
workflows.summary: Appraise the options, model benefits and costs as ranges, compute NPV and payback with sensitivities, and write the case finance will sign.

lenses.note: Buy option priced from the vendor quote.

loops: Sponsor and finance disagree → portfolio board
NPV negative at likely → recommend no-go

contract.definition: Appraise the options, model benefits and costs as ranges, compute NPV and payback with sensitivities, and write the case finance will sign.
recovery: Show low / likely / high and lead with likely
Add three years of licences and support
contract.handoff: Business case, benefits model & options appraisal → 2.5.2 Secure Funding & Resourcing

objectives: Restate the need and the outcomes
Appraise options: do nothing, buy, build, hybrid
Model benefits with ramp-up by site
Model build and run costs from the forecast
lessons.exercise: On your own project, produce Business case and Benefits model and Options appraisal — so that: A business case: options, benefits, costs, NPV and payback as ranges, sensitivities and a benefit owner.
lessons.prompt:
I'm working through "Build the Business Case" (Plan → Investment & Approval) on my own project. Act as my assistant: draft and check, I decide.

Goal: Show, with ranges, why this investment is worth more than its alternatives.
Done looks like: A business case: options, benefits, costs, NPV and payback as ranges, sensitivities and a benefit owner.

I'll attach or paste: Sizing model & sources; Cost estimate; Delivery forecast; Release plan.

Work through these steps with me, one at a time:
1. Appraise options incl. do nothing → Options appraisal
2. Model benefits with ramp-up → Benefits model
3. Model costs; compute NPV & payback → NPV & payback model
4. Run sensitivities → Sensitivity analysis
5. Finance validates the model? (a decision — give me the options and a recommendation; I make the call)
6. Write the business case → Business case

Produce: Business case; Benefits model; Options appraisal. Use clear headings I can paste into my document.

Before you finish, check it against: Ranges for every material input; Do-nothing option included; Benefit owner named; Ranges with sources; Three options including do nothing.

Ask me for anything you need instead of guessing. Keep it specific to my project.

lessons.title: Secure Funding & Resourcing
lessons.summary: Turn the case into money and people, released in tranches against evidence.

definition.purpose: Turn the case into money and people, released in tranches against evidence.
definition.outcome: A funding request and confirmed allocation: tranche-1 budget, team assignment and procurement path.
definition.jtbd: Help me get the money and the team, without asking for everything up front.
exit: Procurement route agreed for vendor spend

normal: Split the investment into tranches tied to evidence milestones
Confirm the budget line with finance
flow.stateTransitions: Requested → Budget confirmed → Team confirmed → Funded (tranche 1)

cases.happyPath: Tranche 1 inside the sponsor's limit; team confirmed.
alternates: Funded from an existing product budget → allocation only
edgeCases: Mid-year licence spend needs CFO approval
The tranche-2 milestone depends on the vendor
exceptions: Budget line frozen → escalate with the cost of delay
failures: Full amount committed up front with no evidence gates

routing.alternate: Funded within a product budget → allocation note only
routing.rework: Request incomplete → back to the case
routing.escalation: Above the sponsor's limit or a new budget line → portfolio board / CFO
routing.stop: Funding refused → stop; park with a revisit trigger — recorded in the learning log

criteria: Tranches tied to measurable evidence milestones
checks: Finance check of the budget line
rules: No spend before funding is confirmed
policies: Delegated authority limits per finance policy

roles: C — Finance partner, Procurement, Engineering lead
execution.authority: Sponsor approves within their limit; portfolio board or CFO above it.

continuity.handoff: Funding request and confirmation → 2.5.3 Confirm Risk, Compliance & Conditions
traceability: Funding linked to BC-## and INI-###; tranches linked to evidence milestones

workflows.title: Request Tranche Funding
workflows.summary: Split the investment into tranches gated by evidence, request tranche 1, confirm budget and team, and start procurement.

lenses.note: Request names budget line and amount.

contract.definition: Split the investment into tranches gated by evidence, request tranche 1, confirm budget and team, and start procurement.
decisions: Is the request within delegated authority and confirmed?
failures: Team not released by line managers
recovery: Re-cut into tranches with evidence milestones
Escalate allocation with the cost of delay
contract.handoff: Funding request & confirmation → 2.5.3 Confirm Risk, Compliance & Conditions

objectives: Split the investment into tranches tied to evidence milestones
Confirm the budget line with finance
lessons.exercise: On your own project, produce Funding request and Funding confirmation — so that: A funding request and confirmed allocation: tranche-1 budget, team assignment and procurement path.
lessons.prompt:
I'm working through "Secure Funding & Resourcing" (Plan → Investment & Approval) on my own project. Act as my assistant: draft and check, I decide.

Goal: Turn the case into money and people, released in tranches against evidence.
Done looks like: A funding request and confirmed allocation: tranche-1 budget, team assignment and procurement path.

I'll attach or paste: Business case; Capacity plan; Release plan.

Work through these steps with me, one at a time:
1. Split into evidence-gated tranches → Tranche plan
2. Prepare the funding request → Funding request
3. Confirm budget line & team → Budget allocation
4. Within authority & confirmed? (a decision — give me the options and a recommendation; I make the call)
5. Raise procurement for vendor spend → Procurement request

Produce: Funding request; Funding confirmation. Use clear headings I can paste into my document.

Before you finish, check it against: Tranches tied to measurable evidence milestones; Funding within delegated authority; Tranches tied to evidence; Within authority.

Ask me for anything you need instead of guessing. Keep it specific to my project.

lessons.title: Confirm Risk, Compliance & Conditions
lessons.summary: Screen risk, privacy, security and vendors, and set the conditions attached to commitment.

definition.purpose: Make sure nothing legal, regulatory, security or vendor-related will stop the commitment later.
definition.outcome: An updated risk register, a compliance and privacy screening, vendor due diligence and the conditions attached to commitment.
definition.jtbd: Help me find what could block us after we've committed, while it's still cheap to deal with.
exit: Residual risk within appetite or escalated
Conditions listed with owners and dates

normal: Refresh the risk register from PLAN outputs
Screen privacy (DPIA need), security and compliance

alternates: DPIA needed → scheduled in DESIGN as a condition before go-live
edgeCases: Vendor processes data outside the EU
exceptions: Legal review late → conditional acceptance with a date
failures: Screening skipped because 'it's an internal tool'

routing.alternate: DPIA required → carried as a condition into DESIGN
routing.escalation: Residual risk above appetite → risk owner / board
routing.stop: Blocking legal or regulatory issue → stop; recommend no-go — recorded in the learning log

criteria: Every condition has an owner and a date
rules: No commitment with an unowned high risk

roles: C — Privacy officer, Security, Legal, Compliance officer
execution.authority: Risk owner accepts residual risk; the board above appetite.

continuity.handoff: Risk register, screenings and commitment conditions → 2.5.4 Make the Commitment Decision
traceability: RSK-## updated; conditions linked to owners and CMT-##

workflows.title: Screen Risk & Set Conditions
workflows.summary: Refresh the risk register, screen privacy, security, compliance and the vendor, and write the conditions the commitment will carry.

lenses.note: DPIA needed? Lawful basis for order data.
Security pre-assessment of the new data flow.
Retention of PDFs and extracted data.
Data residency, SLA and exit terms.
Each condition has an owner and a date.

contract.definition: Refresh the risk register, screen privacy, security, compliance and the vendor, and write the conditions the commitment will carry.
decisions: Is the residual risk within appetite?
cases: Vendor processes data outside the EU
recovery: Run the screening before the commitment meeting
Assign each condition an owner and a date or drop it
contract.handoff: Risk register, screenings & commitment conditions → 2.5.4 Make the Commitment Decision

objectives: Refresh the risk register from PLAN outputs
Screen privacy (DPIA need), security and compliance
lessons.exercise: On your own project, produce Risk register and Compliance & privacy screening and Vendor due-diligence record and Commitment conditions — so that: An updated risk register, a compliance and privacy screening, vendor due diligence and the conditions attached to commitment.
lessons.prompt:
I'm working through "Confirm Risk, Compliance & Conditions" (Plan → Investment & Approval) on my own project. Act as my assistant: draft and check, I decide.

Goal: Make sure nothing legal, regulatory, security or vendor-related will stop the commitment later.
Done looks like: An updated risk register, a compliance and privacy screening, vendor due diligence and the conditions attached to commitment.

I'll attach or paste: Risk register; Requirements baseline; Dependency register.

Work through these steps with me, one at a time:
1. Refresh the risk register → Risk register
2. Screen privacy, security & compliance → Compliance & privacy screening
3. Run vendor due diligence → Vendor due-diligence record
4. Set commitment conditions → Commitment conditions
5. Residual risk within appetite? (a decision — give me the options and a recommendation; I make the call)

Produce: Risk register; Compliance & privacy screening; Vendor due-diligence record; Commitment conditions. Use clear headings I can paste into my document.

Before you finish, check it against: Every risk owned and rated; Every condition has an owner and a date; Every risk owned; Every condition dated.

Ask me for anything you need instead of guessing. Keep it specific to my project.

lessons.title: Make the Commitment Decision
lessons.summary: Go, Phase, Rework, Escalate or No-go — and hand a committed initiative to DESIGN.

definition.purpose: Commit explicitly — Go, Phase, Rework, Escalate or No-go — and hand a complete initiative to DESIGN.
definition.outcome: A signed commitment record (CMT) and, on Go or Phase, the committed-initiative pack handed to DESIGN.
definition.jtbd: Help us commit with our eyes open and leave a record we can be held to.
entry: Business case, funding, conditions and plan complete
exit: On Go / Phase: pack accepted by DESIGN

cases.happyPath: Phase: tranche 1 committed for the MVP and the Rotterdam pilot; tranche 2 on evidence.
exceptions: Decider absent → delegate per the authority matrix
failures: Sunk-cost Go after a weak case

routing.alternate: Phase → commit the first tranche; later tranches return to this gate
routing.rework: Rework → back to the named PLAN process
routing.stop: No-go → decision record, park or close, learning log

criteria: Decision is one of Go, Phase, Rework, Escalate, No-go
rules: No DESIGN or BUILD spend without a commitment record

roles: C — Finance partner, Engineering lead, Risk owner
execution.authority: Sponsor decides within their limit; portfolio board above it or on escalation.

continuity.handoff: Commitment decision record and committed initiative pack → DESIGN; learning log and retrospective → EVOLVE
traceability: Creates CMT-## and LRN-### linking BC, RQ baseline version, RMP and RSK
learning: PLAN retrospective; park revisit dates — learning log

workflows.title: Hold the Commitment Decision
workflows.summary: Put the complete pack in front of the decider, commit explicitly, record the decision with its conditions and hand the committed initiative to DESIGN.

lenses.note: Case, funding and tranche plan in the pack.
Forecast and capacity in the pack.
The right authority is in the room.
Go, Phase, Rework, Escalate or No-go — explicitly.
DESIGN receives baseline, backlog, roadmap and conditions.

loops: Rework → complete the pack / named process

contract.definition: Put the complete pack in front of the decider, commit explicitly, record the decision with its conditions and hand the committed initiative to DESIGN.
decisions: Go, Phase, Rework, Escalate or No-go?
recovery: Reconstruct the record from the minutes the same day
Independent challenge of the Go against the case
exit: On Go / Phase: DESIGN accepts the pack
contract.handoff: Commitment decision record & committed initiative pack → DESIGN (Act III) and Close PLAN & Capture Learning
traceability: CMT-## → BC-##, RQ baseline version, RMP-##

workflows.title: Close PLAN & Capture Learning
workflows.summary: Whatever the decision, capture what planning taught us, set a revisit trigger if parked, and update the portfolio so the initiative's status is true.

lenses.note: Learning recorded against the commitment ID.
Estimate and case accuracy to check in EVOLVE.
Park needs an owner and a revisit trigger.
Trigger tied to a date or measurable condition.

decisions: Was the initiative stopped or parked?
recovery: Portfolio board requires the retro before tranche 2

traceability: Each learning LRN-### linked to CMT-##
learning: Retrospective changes applied to the next PLAN

lessons.prompt:
I'm working through "Make the Commitment Decision" (Plan → Investment & Approval) on my own project. Act as my assistant: draft and check, I decide.

Goal: Commit explicitly — Go, Phase, Rework, Escalate or No-go — and hand a complete initiative to DESIGN.
Done looks like: A signed commitment record (CMT) and, on Go or Phase, the committed-initiative pack handed to DESIGN.

I'll attach or paste: Requirements baseline; Product backlog; Release roadmap; Business case; Funding confirmation; Commitment conditions.

Ask me for anything you need instead of guessing. Keep it specific to my project.
